age.evidence: Male and female (10-16 wk) C57BL/6 J wild-type mice

sex.evidence: Male and female (10-16 wk) C57BL/6 J wild-type mice

dosing.evidence: Mice were dosed intraperitoneally at 0.3, 2, or 10 mg/kg (psilocybin)... in sterile saline
Morphine sulfate... diluted with saline (0.9%) to obtain a working concentration of 1 mg/ml. Mice were dosed intraperitoneally at... 10 mg/kg (morphine)
Buprenorphine was obtained at a concentration of 0.3 mg/mL and diluted to 0.1 mg/mL working concentration... Mice were dosed intraperitoneally at... 1 mg/kg (buprenorphine).

handling.evidence: Methods do not describe a handling habituation protocol.

group_housing.evidence: housed 4-5 per cage in sterile ventilated cages

day_night_flipped.evidence: Animals were maintained on a 12:12 light/dark cycle... All behavior testing took place during the light cycle.

enrichment_housing.evidence: containing Alpha-dri bedding, Enviro-dri enrichment material (Shepherd Specialty Papers)

assays.assay_description: 20-min observation in transparent acrylic arena (68×22×26 cm); trained observer recorded head twitch responses and rearing bouts in 2-min intervals.

application_type.evidence: treated with 0.3, 2, or 10 mg/kg of psilocybin or saline (i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Before experimentation, animals were acclimatized for at least 90 minutes in a dimly lit room... immediately placed in a transparent acrylic arena

setup_restrain.evidence: immediately placed in a transparent acrylic arena... for observation over 20 minutes

food_restriction.evidence: No food in transparent acrylic arena during 20-min observation.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in transparent acrylic arena during 20-min observation.

time_to_assay.evidence: treated... and immediately placed in a transparent acrylic arena for observation over 20 minutes

sample_size.evidence: saline N=10 [7 M/3 F]; 0.3 mg/kg N=6 [3 M/3 F]; 2 mg/kg N=10 [7 M/3 F]; 10 mg/kg N=6 [3 M/3 F]

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin produced a dose-dependent increase in head twitch response and a dose-dependent decrease in rearing bouts.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin (PSI) at 0.3, 2, and 10 mg/kg is physiologically active as shown by quantification of Head Twitch Response... PSI reduces rearing bouts in a dose-dependent manner.

B1_num_measures.evidence: head twitch responses and rearing behaviors recorded

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: One-way ANOVA of total head twitches at the final time point

B4_ethological.evidence: rearing bouts (natural exploratory behaviour) scored as a distinct act

B7_automated_classification.evidence: A trained observer (A.B.C.) recorded head twitch responses and rearing behaviors

E8_food_water.evidence: no food or water in arena

assays.assay_description: Mechanical allodynia assessed using calibrated von Frey filaments applied to lateral plantar region of hind paw via up-down method. Used across SNI, AIMP, and CFA models at 1, 4, and 24 h post-dose during acute and chronic phases.

application_type.evidence: Mice were dosed intraperitoneally at 0.3, 2, or 10 mg/kg (psilocybin)

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were acclimated to the testing chamber for 1-2 days prior to the start of the study (1 h/session). On each testing day, the animals were acclimated in the testing chamber for 1 h.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice in plexiglass enclosures mounted onto a testing platform with a metal, perforated floor

food_restriction.evidence: No food in von Frey testing enclosure.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in von Frey testing enclosure.

time_to_assay.evidence: behavioral assessments at 1, 4, and 24 hours after drug injection during acute and chronic phases

sample_size.evidence: SNI N=12 [6 M/6 F]/group; AIMP groups N=10-14; CFA N=8 [4 M/4 F] per group

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin had no effect on mechanical hypersensitivity in any of the three pain models (SNI, AIMP, CFA) at any dose or time point tested, in acute or chronic phases.
outcomes.evidence: None of the psilocybin doses administered altered the established thermal or mechanical hypersensitivity at any of the acute time points tested.

D1_continuity.evidence: tested at 1, 4, and 24 hours, acute and chronic phases

D2_session_duration.evidence: von Frey trials are brief (session duration not specified beyond 1 h acclimation)

D3_recording_days.evidence: Acute phase tested at 1, 4, 24 h (day 7+) and chronic phase tested 2 weeks later (~day 21+) across pain models

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline for psilocybin reported in this assay

D5_followup.evidence: tested 24 h after injection, plus chronic phase 2 weeks after first dose

assays.assay_description: Radiant heat applied to plantar surface of hind paw; latency to nocifensive response recorded (30 s cut-off). Used across SNI, AIMP, and CFA pain models at 1, 4, and 24 h post-dose during acute and chronic phases.

setup_habituation.evidence: animals acclimatized to the testing environment for 1-2 days prior... 20 min on each testing day

setup_restrain.evidence: plexiglass enclosures on a glass platform

time_to_assay.evidence: tested at 1, 4, and 24 hours after drug injection, acute and chronic phases

sample_size.evidence: SNI N=12/group; AIMP groups N=10-14; CFA N=8/group

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin had no effect on thermal hypersensitivity in any pain model at any dose or time point, except a single isolated effect in females at 0.3 mg/kg in chronic AIMP.
outcomes.evidence: None of the psilocybin doses administered altered the established thermal or mechanical hypersensitivity at any of the acute time points tested.

D1_continuity.evidence: tested at 1, 4, 24 h, plus chronic phase

D2_session_duration.evidence: Hargreaves trials brief (specific duration not reported)

D3_recording_days.evidence: Acute (day 7+) and chronic (~day 21+) phases at three timepoints each

D5_followup.evidence: 24 h post-injection and chronic phase ~2 weeks later

assays.assay_description: Force-sensitive tweezer applied to gastrocnemius muscle of restrained mouse; threshold force to withdrawal recorded over 3 averaged trials. Used in AIMP model at acute and chronic phases.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were acclimated to the behavior room and restraints in two 5-minute sessions over two days

setup_restrain.evidence: the mouse was placed in a gardening glove, and the hind limb was exposed

food_restriction.evidence: no food access during restraint testing

water_restriction.evidence: no water access during restraint testing

time_to_assay.evidence: tested at 1, 4, and 24 hours after drug injection during acute and chronic phases

sample_size.evidence: AIMP CON N=14 [7M/7F]; AIMP+PSI 0.3 N=12; 2 N=12; 10 N=10

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin had no effect on muscle pressure hypersensitivity in the AIMP model at any dose or time point in either acute or chronic phases.
outcomes.evidence: None of the psilocybin doses administered improved cutaneous thermal, muscle pressure, or cutaneous mechanical hypersensitivity in the AIMP model

E1_environment_type.evidence: gardening glove restraint with force-sensitive tweezer

D1_continuity.evidence: tested at 1, 4, 24 h plus chronic phase

D2_session_duration.evidence: three brief trials per session, 2 s force application

D3_recording_days.evidence: acute and chronic phases with multiple timepoints

D5_followup.evidence: 24 h timepoint and chronic phase ~2 weeks later

assays.assay_description: Free access to adjacent temperature-controlled plates (30°C vs 40°C or 30°C vs 20°C) for 5 min; movement tracked with SLEAP and location scored with SimBA.

application_type.evidence: mice were injected with either saline, morphine 10 mg, or psilocybin (0.3, 2, or 10 mg/kg) 60 minutes before testing

setup_habituation.evidence: Methods do not describe apparatus habituation for thermal place preference.

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to move freely for 5 minutes

sample_size.evidence: CON N=6-9; CFA N=13; CFA+MOR N=9; PSI groups N=8-11

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin dose-dependently produced preference for the 40°C plate (both CFA-treated and naive) and avoidance of the 20°C plate. Effect appeared stronger in female mice at 2 and 10 mg/kg, and is interpreted as a consequence of psilocybin-induced hypothermia rather than analgesia.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin-injected mice dose-dependently preferred the 40 °C surface... psilocybin produced a dose-dependent avoidance of a 20 °C surface. This effect appears stronger in female mice at the 2 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg doses.

B1_num_measures.evidence: preference score from time on two plates

B4_ethological.evidence: thermal zone preference is a spatial measure

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Animal movement was tracked using SLEAP version 1.3.3, and location was scored using SimBA version 1.93.4

E6_spatial.evidence: two physically separate temperature plates (30°C and 40°C or 20°C)

assays.assay_description: Mice placed on cold surface and nocifensive responses recorded; performed after formalin injection (acute) and in SNI model at 1, 4, 24 h post-dose during acute and chronic phases.

setup_habituation.evidence: Methods do not specify cold plate habituation.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice placed on cold surface, freely moving

time_to_assay.evidence: Formalin: 30 min post-injection. SNI: tested at 1, 4, and 24 h post-psilocybin in acute and chronic phases.

sample_size.evidence: Formalin groups N=11-12 [6M/6F or 6M/5F]; SNI N=12 [6M/6F] per group

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin dose-dependently decreased formalin-induced cold sensitivity. In the SNI model, no significant dose effect was observed at any acute or chronic timepoint. The apparent acute cold-sensitivity reduction is attributed to psilocybin-induced hypothermia.
outcomes.evidence: acute psilocybin dose-dependently decreased acute formalin-induced cold sensitivity on the cold-plate test. Psilocybin had no significant effect on cold sensitivity in our acute neuropathic pain model (SNI).

D1_continuity.evidence: tested at 1, 4, 24 h after injection in acute and chronic SNI phases

D2_session_duration.evidence: duration not explicitly stated but cold-plate tests are short

D3_recording_days.evidence: acute phase (7 days after SNI) and chronic phase (21 days after SNI) with three time points each

D5_followup.evidence: 24 h post-injection plus chronic phase 2 weeks later

assays.assay_description: Standard cage filled with 5 cm corncob bedding and 25 marbles; mouse placed alone for 15 min; marbles >2/3 buried counted.

setup_habituation.evidence: Methods do not describe marble-burying apparatus habituation.

food_restriction.evidence: no food in test cage during 15-min test

water_restriction.evidence: no water in test cage during test

time_to_assay.evidence: Performed after CFA + psilocybin injection; 'The reduced marble burying effect of psilocybin returned to baseline by 24 hours.'

sample_size.evidence: CON N=14 [7 M/7F]; CFA N=14 [7 M/7 F]; CFA + BUP N=16 [9 M/7F]; CFA + PSI 2 mg/kg N=21 [10 M/11 F]

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (2 mg/kg) reduced marble-burying performance further beyond the CFA-induced decrement; the effect returned to baseline by 24 hours. Buprenorphine increased marble burying.
outcomes.evidence: PSI 2 mg/kg reduces marble burying performance in CFA-treated mice vs control (CON) and CFA + buprenorphine. The reduced marble burying effect of psilocybin returned to baseline by 24 hours.

B4_ethological.evidence: marble burying reflects natural digging/burying behaviour

E1_environment_type.evidence: empty standard habitat with bedding and marbles

E3_bedding.evidence: filled with 5 cm of flat corncob bedding

E5_enrichment.evidence: marbles are test stimuli, not enrichment

D1_continuity.evidence: acute test and 24 h follow-up (returned to baseline by 24 h)

D5_followup.evidence: marble burying effect returned to baseline by 24 hours

assays.assay_description: Automated PainFace facial expression scoring from 10-min videos recorded at baseline and 30 min after laparotomy + drug injection; difference score reported.

application_type.evidence: Animals then received i.p. injection of their assigned experimental compound

setup_habituation.evidence: Methods describe baseline recording before surgery but do not explicitly state separate apparatus habituation.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in a plastic enclosure and recorded

food_restriction.evidence: no food in plastic recording enclosure

water_restriction.evidence: no water in plastic recording enclosure

time_to_assay.evidence: 30 minutes after completing laparotomy and receiving saline or drug injection, mice were recorded for a second 10 minute session

sample_size.evidence: SAL N=12 [6M/6F]; BUP 1 mg/kg N=11 [7M/4F]; PSI 2 mg/kg N=14 [7M/7F]

outcomes.summary: Buprenorphine significantly reduced post-laparotomy grimace scale, whereas psilocybin (2 mg/kg) had no effect on the mouse grimace scale.
outcomes.statistics: F(2,33)=4.535, P=0.0182; Tukey post-hoc P<0.05 versus SAL and PSI 2 mg/kg
outcomes.evidence: BUP 1 mg/kg, but not PSI 2 mg/kg, reduces mouse grimace scale score after laparotomy.

B4_ethological.evidence: facial expressions reveal spontaneous ongoing affective component of pain

B7_automated_classification.evidence: automated machine learning analysis tool PainFace... automatically scored using the default C57BL/6 model

D4_baseline.evidence: mice were placed in a plastic enclosure and recorded for 10 minutes to establish a baseline score

judge_notes: Merged candidates' separate Hargreaves/von Frey/MWT/cold plate assays across SNI, AIMP, CFA models into single per-paradigm assay entries, per rubric rule that same test across pain-model cohorts = 1 assay.

Added Body Temperature (thermal imaging) as a distinct assay — it is a behavioural-arena-based recording with SLEAP-based body tracking, time-course (one-minute bins) reported, and is the primary outcome of Fig. 4. gptoss omitted it; qwen omitted it.

Added Morphine and Buprenorphine as separate dosing entries because the rubric says to capture every drug COMPOUND administered to animals in the behavioural experiments (these are comparators in the same assays as psilocybin).
B4 (ethological): scored Yes for marble burying (digging/burying) and grimace (natural facial expressions) following rubric examples; rearing in HTR arena scored Yes as natural exploratory behaviour.

D3 recording days for the chronic-pain assays scored 8-14 because each assay was run on the SNI/AIMP/CFA cohorts at 1 h, 4 h, and 24 h timepoints in both acute (~day 7) and chronic (~day 21) phases — multiple recording days across both phases.
Setup habituation for thermal place preference, marble burying, cold plate, and grimace marked 'not_reported' rather than 'no' because methods are silent on apparatus pre-exposure.

D2 session duration for von Frey, Hargreaves, MWT, cold plate set to <15 min (score 0) because the actual stimulation/measurement session is brief; the 1-h acclimation is pre-test and not the recording session itself.
